newsitem.title: UK: SFA calls for shake-up of regulatory system - paper.
newsitem.headline: SFA calls for shake-up of regulatory system - paper.

text.p: The head of the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA), Richard Farrant, has called for a shake-up of the regulatory system to create a single powerful regulator to govern banks, fund managers and investment banks, the Financial Times (FT) said on Monday.
The FT said Farrant made the comments in an interview in which he described the existing regulatory structure as becoming "antiquated".
At present banking supervision lies with the Bank of England, with securities houses and investment banks coming under the control of the SFA and its overseer the Securities and Investment Board.

Farrant's comments follow the Bank of England insisting that it will retain responsibility for banking regulation. Farrant said he would be willing for the central bank to take on securities regulation as well.
But the comments coincide with a study published on Monday which calls for banking supervision to be taken away from the Bank of England, the FT said.
The study, by Michael Taylor who was a former central bank official, instead calls for a Financial Stability Commission to be created.
This could lead to the scrapping of the SIB, the overarching financial regulator, transfering its powers and those of the central bank and other regulators including the SFA to the new Commission.
